rule.description: An inlined item-size limit guard is a threshold comparison (>, >=, <, <=) in which one side measures the size of the stored value (a .length / .size member access, a byteLength() / X.byteLength() call, or a local alias initialized from such a measurement) and the other side is a non-literal limit expression. The stored-value size limit policy is one responsibility: when two or more owner files each re-implement the guard inline, a conceptual change to the policy (unit of measurement, limit resolution, reaction) requires coordinated edits in every owner, which is the shotgun surgery relation.

checks.description: Detect each driver owner that re-implements the stored-value size limit policy inline as its own threshold comparison instead of delegating to a single owning module.
checks.detected_relation: driver write path -> per-owner inline copy of the value-size limit policy
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Every driver keeps its own copy of the same conceptual write guard, expressed with its own measurement form (character count, UTF-8 encoding length, byteLength helper, Blob size) and its own reaction (silent skip or thrown error). Unifying the unit, moving the limit, or changing the failure mode therefore requires the same conceptual edit to be rediscovered and repeated in every owner file — the definition of shotgun surgery. Consolidating the guard (and the option typing) into one shared owner removes the matches.

matches.evidence: setItem guards the write with its own inline comparison `value.length > options.maxItemSize` and silently skips oversized values.
setItemRaw duplicates the setItem guard inline (`value.length > options.maxItemSize`) with the same silent-skip reaction.
setItem measures `value.length` against `opts.maxItemSize` inline and throws a driver-specific quota error of its own wording.
setItem stores `const size = new TextEncoder().encode(value).length` and compares that alias against `opts.maxItemSize` inline with its own error message.
setItemRaw repeats the TextEncoder measurement and comparison (`size > opts.maxItemSize`) inline.
setItem applies its own inline guard `byteLength(value) > opts.maxItemSize` using the lru-cache byteLength helper.
setItemRaw duplicates the byteLength-based guard inline, silently skipping oversized writes.

A driver-local closure `checkLength` implements the policy with `value.length <= opts?.maxItemSize` (bounds check inverted so the non-violating path returns early) and throws a driver-worded error from both write paths.
setItem measures the request body via `const bodySize = new Blob([value]).size` and compares that alias against `opts.maxItemSize` inline.
setItemRaw repeats the Blob-size measurement and inline comparison before uploading.
setItem applies its own inline guard `Buffer.byteLength(value) > opts.maxItemSize` and throws a driver-worded error instead of writing the file.
setItemRaw duplicates the Buffer.byteLength guard inline before writing raw content to disk.

setItem resolves the limit as `const maxItemSize = topts?.maxItemSize ?? opts.maxItemSize` (per-call override of the driver option) and guards inline with `value.length > maxItemSize` before the KV put; this is the only owner with per-call limit resolution.

measurement.limit_form: non-literal identifier holding per-call or driver option

excluded.description: Comparisons that constitute a For/While/DoWhile loop test, such as `i < keys.length` in src/drivers/s3.ts deleteObjects.
excluded.why: These compare iteration position against collection length; they bound traversal, not a configurable stored-value size policy.

excluded.description: Size comparisons against numeric literals, such as `value.length > 0` presence checks.
excluded.why: A hardcoded literal bound is not a configurable policy that owners can silently drift apart on, so it is not the scattered size policy relation.

excluded.description: Comparisons in which both sides measure, such as `base.length > mountpoint.length` in src/storage.ts.
excluded.why: Both sides are measurements of the same kind; no configurable limit expression is involved.

excluded.description: Numeric driver options that do not measure stored-value content (TTL seconds, LRU maxSize in number of entries, cloudflare-kv minTTL), including their pass-through to underlying libraries.
excluded.why: The rule's measured side must measure the stored value itself; entry-count and time budgets pass `value.length`-style tests only trivially and are not flagged.
